language.script_notes: Devanagari script dominates across the Hindi Belt (UP, Bihar, MP, Rajasthan, Delhi, Haryana); Gurmukhi script appears in Punjab specifically. Both are visually distinct from the South's Dravidian scripts.
false_friends: Pakistan (shared Punjab region, split by partition)
South India (same country, very different script/architecture)

road_furniture.curb_style: As national; dense, chaotic mixed traffic especially pronounced in the Delhi-NCR region.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national, including the distinctive unofficial low-quality camera coverage in many areas.

architecture.roof_style: Flat concrete roofs as national default; Nagara-style Hindu temples feature a curved, beehive-shaped shikhara tower over the sanctum — the defining North Indian temple architectural signature.
architecture.roof_material: Flat poured concrete as national default.
architecture.wall_construction: Sandstone and marble palace/fort architecture historic in Rajasthan (Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur); dense concrete urban construction in Delhi and the Gangetic cities; Sikh gurdwara architecture with white domes in Punjab.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Rajasthan's 'Pink City' (Jaipur) and 'Blue City' (Jodhpur) carry distinctive painted old-town palettes; otherwise mixed grey concrete and painted shopfronts nationwide.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Nagara-style Hindu temples with curved shikhara towers; Mughal-era architecture (domes, minarets, red sandstone forts — Taj Mahal, Red Fort); Rajasthani palace and fort architecture; white-domed Sikh gurdwaras in Punjab.

nature.vegetation: The fertile Indo-Gangetic Plain supports intensive agriculture (wheat, rice, sugarcane) with subtropical deciduous trees (sal, neem, peepal, banyan); the Thar Desert in western Rajasthan brings sandy dunes and sparse thorn-forest vegetation (babool, ber).
nature.terrain: Overwhelmingly flat, intensively farmed alluvial plain fed by the Ganges and its tributaries; the Thar Desert in the west; the Himalayan foothills rise abruptly along the northern edge.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, dry and dusty for much of the year with a hazy quality to much outdoor imagery; intensely green during and after the monsoon; noticeably drier and sandier in Rajasthan specifically.

vehicles.plate_color: As national — Delhi ('DL'), Punjab ('PB'), Rajasthan ('RJ'), Uttar Pradesh ('UP') state codes.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: As national; camel and bullock carts still visible on rural Rajasthani roads.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of official Google coverage in Delhi/major cities and the distinctive unofficial 'foggy' camera elsewhere, as national.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense around Delhi-NCR; more variable quality across rural Rajasthan/UP/Bihar.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Punjab region geography and culture straddling the partition-era border, similar Indo-Gangetic terrain
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Pakistan uses Urdu in Perso-Arabic script and drives on the left same as India, but Pakistani plates and road signage differ; Indian Punjab uses Gurmukhi script (for Sikh Punjabi) which doesn't appear in Pakistani Punjab's Urdu-dominant signage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same general road furniture and flat-concrete-roof default
confusion_set.tiebreaker: North India uses Devanagari/Gurmukhi script with Nagara-style curved-tower temples; South India uses Dravidian scripts with distinctive pyramid-shaped gopuram temple gateways — an unmistakable difference once either is visible.
